headline.purpose: Reserved for LoginView.vue's hero copy -- the one screen in this app closer to Persuade than Operate. Not used for routine page titles.

title.purpose: This app's workhorse heading -- the 'where you are' size at the top of every list/settings/detail screen.

label.purpose: Form labels, buttons, table headers, compact UI text -- the most-used size in a dense operate-mode app.

caption.purpose: Helper text, inline validation, status-badge labels, timestamps.

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Resting elevation for AppCard or the primary button at rest. Reconciled from provider-panel's prior --shadow-panel.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Hover/emphasis elevation -- primary button hover, and the floating AppSelect dropdown panel (currently mis-tiered onto shadow-sm).

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Highest-elevation surface -- modal/sheet overlays. Reconciled from provider-panel's prior --shadow-pop.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Tactile press-down feedback on :active for buttons, inherited from user-app's BaseButton.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition duration for button color/shadow/transform changes.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action on a screen -- accent fill, deepens on hover. Not yet a shared component in this app (every page currently hand-rolls this markup); this is the target to extract an AppButton toward.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; background: var(--color-accent); color: #FFFFFF; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.875rem; padding: 10px 16px; border-radius: 12px; border: none; box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); transition: all 150ms; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--color-accent-strong); box-shadow: var(--shadow-md); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--color-accent); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.6; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Signature component of this app, already implemented well (StatusBadge.vue) -- pill badge with a leading dot, tone-mapped across success/warning/danger/info/neutral. A candidate to back-port to user-app and admin-panel rather than something to fix here.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; padding: 4px 10px; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; } .ds-badge-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: currentColor; } .ds-badge-warning { background: var(--color-warning-soft); color: var(--color-warning); }

components.name: Card
components.description: AppCard.vue -- already correctly on-token (16px radius, bordered, flat-at-rest shadow).
components.css: .ds-card { border-radius: 16px; border: 1px solid var(--color-border); background: var(--color-surface-card); box-shadow: var(--shadow-sm); padding: 16px; } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--color-text); margin-bottom: 8px; } .ds-card-body { font-size: 1rem; color: var(--color-text-muted); }

narrative.northStar: The Verified Ledger (inherited from apps/user-app -- see that app's design.json for the full narrative; this file records only what's specific to the Operate-mode provider panel)
narrative.overview: The salon owner's side of the same trust-legible-at-a-glance system user-app builds for customers. Where user-app occasionally leans Persuade (the login hero, salon showcase), this app is almost entirely Operate: scanability and fast task completion for a between-clients phone check, or a longer focused desktop session for setup and earnings review. The accent is used even more sparingly here than in user-app -- a dashboard screen typically has one primary action, sometimes none.
keyCharacteristics: Same two-mode teal/violet re-theme as user-app -- not an independently chosen palette.
Denser default spacing than user-app's baseline -- this is a utility console, not a discovery/marketing surface.
A genuinely good status-badge pattern (StatusBadge.vue) this app has that user-app doesn't yet -- worth sharing back, not fixing.
The token layer is currently incomplete relative to user-app (no accent-strong/deep/soft/text) -- the single biggest gap between this document's target and current code.

rules.name: The One Seal Rule
rules.body: The accent color appears on the single most important element of a screen -- on a dashboard/list screen this is often the one primary action in the header, sometimes none.

rules.name: The No Mode-Agnostic Color Rule
rules.body: Every color in this system has a distinct light and dark value.

rules.name: The Fill-Text Split Rule
rules.body: A 'strong' accent/danger shade verified for white text on top of it as a fill is not automatically safe as foreground text on a card background -- measure and tokenize both directions separately (accent-strong vs accent-text).

rules.name: The Density-First Rule
rules.body: Default to compact spacing; this app has essentially no Persuade-mode screens other than the login hero.

rules.name: The Elevation-Means-Something Rule
rules.body: A shadow is never decorative -- flat + bordered is the default resting state.

rules.name: The Hue-Tinted Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow is never neutral black, even in dark mode -- it carries the mode's accent hue. Provider-panel's current dark-mode shadow (pure rgba(0,0,0,...)) violates this.

rules.name: The Container-Softer-Than-Control Rule
rules.body: A container's radius is one step larger than the controls it holds -- 16px cards, 12px buttons/inputs.

rules.name: The No Physical-Direction Leak Rule
rules.body: Use logical properties (start-/end-), never left/right. LoginView.vue's input icon is a confirmed current violation.

dos: Do treat apps/user-app/DESIGN.md as the parent document -- when a rule isn't restated here, it still governs.
Do build a shared AppButton/AppInput rather than hand-rolling markup per page (currently 31 raw buttons, 34 raw inputs across 15 files).
Do pair a shadow-depth change with a color change on the primary button's hover state.
Do keep the warning/info semantic additions -- a legitimate Operate-mode need, not drift.
Do use logical CSS properties for positioned elements.
donts: Don't treat provider-panel's current --color-border/--color-muted/danger/success hex values as an equally-valid alternative to user-app's -- they are unintentional drift and should be corrected to match exactly.
Don't use pure black for a dark-mode shadow.
Don't invent a third, independently-designed status-tone vocabulary in admin-panel later -- reach for this app's warning/info additions instead.
Don't add a second accent color or spread accent emphasis across more than one element per screen.
